title: CATS-004 Complete bot submission intake over merged foundation
body:
## Synchronized status — 2026-10-18

Next core implementation issue. PR #16 supplies submission services; PRs #24/#27 supply reply placement and truthful cross-provider provenance. Remaining work is bot intake and durable intent recovery. Acceptance ends at pending acknowledgement; #8 owns the inspection-channel projection and decisions, and #7 owns destination delivery.

Baseline: merged main `f63d382`; [PR #27](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/pull/27) completes #6. This update reconciles planning only; unchecked implementation acceptance remains unfinished.

Part of [Epic #1](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/issues/1). See [docs/ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) - Phase 2 - Cat Submission Domain.

## Delivery priority

P1 bot-integration gap. The source-aware service foundation merged in PR #16; the reply graph merged in PR #24. Complete authenticated intake over those services.

## Scope

The source-aware entity/service foundation is implemented. This issue remains open for the missing Telegram bot intake and durable placement-intent integration; manual `/download` and `/publish` do not satisfy this scope.

## Source identity policy

Normalize available source metadata into:

- `source_provider`
- `source_media_id`
- stable `source_channel_id`, when verified
- mutable `source_channel_name` and `source_channel_username`
- source identity status such as `verified`, `user_selected`, or `unresolved`

A third-party downloader caption, button label, display name, or username is not sufficient proof of stable identity. If the backend cannot supply a verified stable source ID, require an explicit logical-thread selection instead of guessing.

## Completed foundation acceptance (PR #16)

- [x] `CatVideoSubmission` has an internal identity and explicit lifecycle state.
- [x] Supported video metadata, source metadata, validation results, and provenance are modeled.
- [x] The service accepts validated local media and Telegram-native media references through explicit input contracts.
- [x] Telegram/Telethon handoff messages are correlated with a one-use internal request token; unrelated messages are rejected.
- [x] Valid submissions are persisted through a repository contract.
- [x] Invalid media, unresolved required source identity, and duplicate source media fail with typed application errors.
- [x] No domain API treats a Telegram message ID, source display name, or username as submission/thread identity.
- [x] Tests cover verified identity, changed display metadata, explicit manual thread selection, unresolved identity, duplicate media, and repository failure.

## Dependencies

#3/#4 and #6 are complete. PR #27 merged the provenance/authorized-placement correction; it is no longer a blocker. Publication belongs to #7 and durable moderation to #8; neither is required to accept intake alone.

## Out of scope

Reimplementing graph decisions, Telegram channel delivery, moderation decisions and production controls. Intake passes stored internal parent selection to the existing #6 service.


## Remaining bot-intake acceptance

- [ ] Real aiogram routing accepts supported media in the authorized private pilot; preserve admin/private restrictions until an explicit access-policy change.
- [ ] A trusted adapter authenticates Telegram input, fetches the actual media bytes and validates through MediaService before constructing internal validation evidence. Never deserialize external assertions as trusted evidence.
- [ ] Normalize Telegram identity with file_unique_id; enforce curated provenance, size/duration limits and secret-safe errors.
- [ ] Reuse SubmissionService for source resolution and one-use actor/conversation-bound handoff handling. Unverified source identity prompts explicit authorized selection of its own source chain using internal IDs; that choice does not fabricate media-source provenance. Cross-provider placement is limited to an already authorized exact-parent entry.
- [ ] Translate normal submission versus an already authorized opaque-token exact-parent entry into the corresponding durable #6 PostIntent. Do not finalize while awaiting approval; do not select an early normal tail or overwrite an exact parent.
- [ ] Make retries/replayed updates recover the existing submission/intent without duplication, including failure between submission persistence and intent creation. Do not imply a transaction spans media acquisition.
- [ ] Keep handlers thin, persist internal IDs only, and preserve cancel/reset/command-replacement rules.
- [ ] Return a clear intake/pending result and expose an application handoff to #7/#8; do not claim publication or moderation is implemented by intake.
- [ ] Real Dispatcher.feed_update tests with fake transport cover both entry modes, native/local validated media, explicit source selection, duplicate/replayed input, invalid media, authorization, persistence failure, cancellation and superseded entry.

The full intake -> approval -> publication flow is accepted across #5/#7/#8, not by adding further records alone.


## Command modularity and pilot robustness gates

- [ ] `/post` is the primary UX; `/submit`, if retained, is an alias of the same workflow. Bare `/post` replaces stale context and prompts for explicit normal placement/target selection, then one video.
- [ ] `/start catreply_<opaque-token>` resolves and authorizes an exact target and opens the same awaiting-media flow directly. No extra `/post` step or raw channel/message-ID arguments. Preserve the target across a slow transfer and later pending review.
- [ ] Introduce focused common/post/media/pilot router factories incrementally, with shared DI, authorization, operation logging, flow leases and the outer error boundary. No SQL, tail decisions or generic retry loops in handlers; no speculative plugin framework.
- [ ] Reuse the corrected #6 policy for authorized exact-parent Telegram uploads under YouTube-source parents. Keep actual provider/file_unique_id and curated provenance unchanged; target thread/parent assignment is placement evidence, not source evidence. Normal append remains source-matched.
- [ ] Replay first reconciles the private inbound projection and existing intent before another transfer. A committed submission plus missing intent resumes only intent creation; mismatched mode/parent or ownership is a typed conflict.
- [ ] Add allowlisted post/intake phase, outcome, safe category, correlation, duration, attempt/recovery logging. No payloads, captions, raw tokens, Telegram IDs, paths, credentials or exception messages; test log redaction and failed error notifications.
- [ ] Typed validation/authorization failures render actionable prompts. Expected persistence uncertainty reconciles first; retries are bounded and repeat-safe. Cancellation drains acquisition/UoW cleanup and preserves the primary error.
- [ ] Real dispatcher/fake transport regressions cover `/post`/alias, old button, replacement/cancel/timeout/restart, cross-provider exact reply, explicit selection, duplicate update and failure after each durable boundary. Add sanitized pilot incidents as reviewed offline regressions before fixes.

Intake still ends at pending acknowledgement: no finalize_intent, channel send, moderation decision or reply-button creation. Admin/private restrictions remain unchanged. No new database backend or automatic live retry is authorized by this plan.

title: CATS-015 Gate YouTube API discovery on multi-owner policy and data-retention approval
body:
## Current execution disposition — 2026-11-26

**Priority:** P0 — independent policy / live-use gate  
**Reviewed `main`:** [`1d066c1`](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/commit/1d066c1e30b91798f642c2b28666ed72f5e56bdf). November 15 [merge CI](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/actions/runs/43737472423) passed then, **not** a new November 26 qualification.  
**Disposition:** **OPEN; written determination remains pending.** The [merged policy memo](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/blob/ad653687a91e9b0a2c4c770bc23606fadebe5cbf/docs/discovery/YOUTUBE_API_POLICY_AND_RETENTION.md) records **written clearance required** for the proposed single operator queue spanning unrelated content owners. No written permitting determination or newly authorized live ingestion evidence is in the reviewed repository. The recorded interpretation must be rechecked against provider terms before any live use.

### Outstanding acceptance — next implementable slice

- [ ] Document the exact proposed service flow: separately owned channels, shared operator audience, identity joins, enrichment, classification, ordering/ranking, persistence and publication bridge. Obtain a written provider decision on **that exact flow**, not generic API access.
- [ ] If the flow is disallowed or remains ambiguous, record a denied/deferred decision and evaluate creator-supplied originals or a genuinely authorized provider. No silent fallback to browser scraping/yt-dlp.
- [ ] If permitting clearance is obtained, freeze per-field provenance and TTL/refresh/deletion requirements, revocation handling and restored-backup read suppression with tests owned by #20.
- [ ] Require a separate owner authorization for bounded deployment-host requests (source, budget, route, time, credentials, evidence retention, abort conditions). A policy decision alone does not authorize a live call.
- [ ] Keep copyright/redistribution rights separate from API-data permission and publishing approval. #22 must verify media acquisition rights independently.

### Ownership, gates and dependencies

Blocking for **production API-backed resolver/lookup/listing/retention and four-hour live scheduling** in #18/#19/#20/#21. Does not block offline synthetic development or manual permitted Telegram submissions. Retain source memo's historical conclusion; do not claim updated legal verification.

**Evidence boundary:** Source integration, offline fixtures, live access, policy authorization and production activation remain distinct decisions. Fresh CI on any final changed head is required; coordinate stale project-context evidence with [#61](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/issues/61).

---

<details><summary>Previously recorded scope and historical acceptance (preserved)</summary>

## Pending determination — 2026-11-15

The [merged decision memo](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/blob/ad653687a91e9b0a2c4c770bc23606fadebe5cbf/docs/discovery/YOUTUBE_API_POLICY_AND_RETENTION.md) records **requires written clearance before production use** for one operator queue spanning unrelated content owners. The next evidence is a written determination on that exact flow, including its audience, joins, ranking and classification, followed by review of refresh, expiry, deletion, revocation and restore controls. Record the determination in the memo and keep production ingestion gated while it is pending.

## Goal

Determine whether CatsChannel may lawfully and contractually use YouTube Data API Services to discover and aggregate metadata for a watchlist containing unrelated creators, and define enforceable retention, refresh and deletion rules before any production API-backed discovery is enabled.

This is a blocking policy-qualification issue, not a conclusion that the proposed use is already permitted or prohibited.

## Why this is a separate gate

The proposed watchlist spans multiple independent channel owners. YouTube's API Services Developer Policies contain restrictions concerning aggregation of API Data across different content owners. The project must not assume that a private application, creator permission to redistribute a video, or a hashed identifier automatically removes those restrictions.

The API policies also impose refresh/deletion requirements for API Data, including a general 30-calendar-day rule and defined exceptions. The exact treatment of each field, authorized/non-authorized data category, derived value and retained identifier must be established before the ledger is designed for indefinite retention.

Official sources to review and pin in the decision record:

- [YouTube API Services Developer Policies](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies)
- [YouTube API Services Terms of Service](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/api-services-terms-of-service)
- [YouTube Data API playlistItems resource](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/playlistItems)
- [YouTube Data API channels resource](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/channels)

## Scope

1. Map the intended CatsChannel use case to the current API policies and terms:
   - one application/operator;
   - multiple unrelated creators and channel owners;
   - public metadata retrieved without user credentials;
   - any future OAuth/user-authorized access;
   - creator permission to redistribute media versus permission to use/aggregate API Data.
2. Obtain and record an authoritative interpretation for the multi-owner aggregation use case. If the published terms do not resolve it, seek written guidance from YouTube/Google or qualified counsel before production use.
3. Produce a field-level data inventory for channel IDs, video IDs, titles, descriptions, publication timestamps, playlist membership, uploader identity, classification, URLs, cursors, quota/error records, derived values and hashes.
4. Define retention and deletion behavior for each category:
   - applicable refresh/delete deadline;
   - whether refresh is permitted and how it is performed;
   - behavior when a channel becomes inaccessible or authorization is revoked;
   - deletion of cached, derived and backup copies where required;
   - whether any minimal deduplication tombstone is permitted;
   - safe operational logging without retaining prohibited API Data.
5. Record the permitted architecture and explicit prohibited alternatives. Do not treat scraping, undocumented endpoints, cookies, proxy rotation or yt-dlp as automatic fallbacks.
6. Identify a compliant alternative if the API use case is not permitted, such as creator-provided original media, a separately authorized link-only workflow, or a metadata provider with appropriate rights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reviewed decision memo exists at `docs/discovery/YOUTUBE_API_POLICY_AND_RETENTION.md`.
- [ ] The memo cites current official policy/terms and records the review date and policy version or retrieval date.
- [ ] The multi-owner aggregation question has an explicit outcome: approved with conditions, requires additional written approval, or not approved.
- [ ] Creator redistribution permission and YouTube API-data permission are treated as separate questions.
- [ ] A field-level retention matrix covers API Data, derived data, identifiers/hashes, cursors, logs, caches and backups; it records refresh, deletion and revocation behavior.
- [ ] The design does not assume that a private deployment or hashing makes otherwise restricted data exempt.
- [ ] The resulting constraints are reflected in #18, #19, #20, #21 and #22.
- [ ] No production API calls, credential changes, live YouTube navigation, scraping or scheduled ingestion are performed as part of this issue without separate explicit authorization and a policy-approved test plan.

## Blocking relationships

- **#18 / CATS-010:** offline resolver fixtures and protocol work may proceed; live API resolution is blocked until this decision permits it.
- **#19 / CATS-011:** provider implementation may proceed against synthetic fixtures; live API-backed enumeration and UUSH qualification are blocked.
- **#20 / CATS-012:** generic ledger work may proceed, but API-data retention, indefinite deduplication and production ingestion must implement this issue's decision.
- **#21 / CATS-013:** no four-hour production schedule until the provider, ledger, retention controls and live one-shot qualification are accepted.
- **#22 / CATS-014:** redistribution rights and YouTube API policy are separate gates; automatic media acquisition remains disabled by default.
- **#17:** this issue is a prerequisite for production API-backed discovery, not for offline engineering.

## Out of scope

- Implementing a provider or database migration.
- Requesting or storing API credentials.
- Performing live YouTube probes.
- Downloading, submitting, moderating or publishing media.
- Treating this issue as legal advice or as approval to operate.

Related: #17, #18, #19, #20, #21, #22.

Policy review (2026-11-12) is recorded in [PR #48's decision memo](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/blob/634c0a1/docs/discovery/YOUTUBE_API_POLICY_AND_RETENTION.md). Written clearance for the proposed operator queue and review of retention controls remain open. Synthetic engineering can proceed; live qualification remains separately gated.


</details>

title: CATS-006 Add Telegram publishing adapter
body:
## Current execution disposition — 2026-11-26

**Priority:** P0 — publication policy / safety fence  
**Reviewed `main`:** [`1d066c1`](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/commit/1d066c1e30b91798f642c2b28666ed72f5e56bdf). [Post-merge CI](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/actions/runs/43737472423) passed on November 15; this is **historical CI evidence**, not fresh November 26 verification.  
**Disposition:** **OPEN; implemented publisher, incomplete release acceptance.** PR #29 provides durable publication, attempt ownership and unknown-send handling; PR #39 documents bounded private exact-parent publication. In the current `bot/handlers.py`, legacy `/publish` still invokes `bot.copy_message` directly. `/pilot_publish` invokes `approve_pilot`; its pilot authorization also needs explicit policy fencing.

### Outstanding acceptance — next implementable slice

- [ ] Define a single publishing-authority contract for approved durable publication versus explicitly authorized private pilot operations. Disallow legacy `/publish` outside verified pilot mode; never leave a direct Telegram send as a production bypass.
- [ ] Gate `/pilot_publish` by explicit verified-private pilot settings and admin authorization; test disabled, wrong admin/chat, wrong destination, and configuration fail-closed cases.
- [ ] Retain review approval, durable attempt ownership, parent placement and idempotent/unknown-send reconciliation for production requests. Never retry ambiguous sends blindly.
- [ ] Qualify actual reply-button navigation and submitter acknowledgement, including restart, missing markup, stale pending attempts, and duplicate callback handling.
- [ ] Record a narrowly scoped private end-to-end receipt and a separate public-release acceptance; do not treat PR #39's bounded receipt as sustained production evidence.

### Ownership, gates and dependencies

Co-own the **publication-policy fence** with #8; operational supervision and recovery are #9. No new YouTube dependency. Preserve existing #29/#39 acceptance and the private-only boundary.

**Evidence boundary:** Merged code/offline tests are not public deployment, live provider authorization, or sustained operational acceptance. For any source merge, obtain fresh checks on the final reviewed head; coordinate date-sensitive project-context repair with [#61](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/issues/61).

title: CATS-007 Add moderation workflow
body:
## Current execution disposition — 2026-11-26

**Priority:** P0 — moderation and publication authority  
**Reviewed `main`:** [`1d066c1`](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/commit/1d066c1e30b91798f642c2b28666ed72f5e56bdf). [Post-merge CI](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/actions/runs/43737472423) passed on November 15; this is **historical CI evidence**, not fresh November 26 verification.  
**Disposition:** **OPEN; approval, audited rejection, and fail-closed startup are merged.** #36 approval, #42 rejection, #43 startup isolation are implemented and offline tested. Public moderation readiness, legacy-pilot policy and reliable notification repair remain incomplete.

### Outstanding acceptance — next implementable slice

- [ ] Define review eligibility and delivery state transitions that permit exactly one terminal approval or rejection, with operator authorization and durable audit.
- [ ] Enforce shared release policy with #7: legacy `/publish` must not bypass review and `/pilot_publish` must remain bounded to an explicitly authorized private pilot. Verify denied paths produce zero sends.
- [ ] Reconcile review-queue delivery, callback markup, missing/duplicate submitter notifications, restart, cancellation and operator repair without reversing a committed decision.
- [ ] Prove approve/reject races and idempotency under SQLite and disposable PostgreSQL, including no logical post or publication after terminal rejection.
- [ ] Accept private review/notification recovery separately from public deployment; avoid automatic publication when review delivery is uncertain.

### Ownership, gates and dependencies

#7 owns durable publication and legacy direct-send fencing; #9 owns supervisor/restart and operational recovery; #22 must reuse the established moderated submission path. Existing bounded private receipt remains historical.

**Evidence boundary:** Merged code/offline tests are not public deployment, live provider authorization, or sustained operational acceptance. For any source merge, obtain fresh checks on the final reviewed head; coordinate date-sensitive project-context repair with [#61](https://github.com/SoloMidMiram/CatsChannel/issues/61).

title: feat: add offline four-hour discovery scheduler
body:
Part of #21. This is the offline scheduling slice.

- Invoke the existing one-shot scanner for UTC four-hour slots with an injected clock and stable slot cycle IDs.
- Guard against overlapping ticks on one scheduler instance. Attempt at most two due slots per tick by default, oldest first, and leave the rest pending.
- Preserve the interrupted slot on cancellation or scanner-wide failure. The scanner retains its existing channel isolation and checkpoint ownership.
- Test six slots per UTC day, disabled and overlapping calls, bounded catch-up, cancellation and retry, and durable cursor recovery with a failed channel alongside a successful channel.

Scheduling state is in memory. A caller can reconstruct it from a saved next slot. Cross-process ownership, durable scheduling state and host activation are outside this slice. Production still requires #51 clearance and separately authorized live qualification.

Refs #7. Keep this PR in draft for review; do not merge automatically.

## Durable delivery and recovery

- Migration `0005_durable_publication` adds unique post/destination publications, versioned attempt ownership, safe outcomes and independent markup state, plus a unique destination projection index.
- Shared per-thread application coordination and database CAS prevent duplicate claims. Sending ownership commits before media reads or Telegram calls; confirmation and projection commit together afterward.
- Timeout, disconnect, cancellation, abandoned sending, invalid coordinates and post-send commit failure remain unknown/non-retryable. Existing legacy projections require operator review without another send. No lease expiry or automatic unknown retry exists.
- A local operator recovery command supports independently verified confirmation, proven non-delivery, explicit requeue and markup-only repair while the bot is stopped.
- The production adapter preflights bot-usable native file IDs, checks bounded trusted library bytes, uses exact `ReplyParameters` without fallback, and sends no source captions/forwarded attribution.
- Managed token rotation is atomic and bounded to one token per publication. Latest confirmed direct-reply navigation uses destination-only channel links; markup repair never resends media.
